text:
alyssa: Heads-up — CI perf test on the streaming suite (p95 end-to-end) regressed ~12% after the rollout this morning. Canarys were paused automatically.

deploy-bot: Canary pause: rollout v2.18.3 -> paused due to p95 regression (alert id: stream-p95-2026-03-18).

samir: saw the same in dashboards, SSE tail latency spikes correlate with tool-call paths. 99th token latency up too. No obvious increase in request rate.

jia: I pulled a flamegraph from the canary pod. Quick summary: serialization time in the eventstream worker jumped ~30ms on average, and there are frequent GC-ish pauses in the KV cache thread around eviction windows.

jia: Paste of the minimized flame summary: 
```
eventstream_write -> serialize_frame (+30ms)
serialize_frame -> pack_tool_call -> serialize_args (+18ms)
kv_cache_eviction -> lock_wait (+12ms, frequent)
kernel_autoselect -> choose_kernel -> compile_path (+8ms for some sequences)
```

alyssa: Interesting — kernel_autoselect changed last week (PR 4321) to prefer the new batching-friendly kernel for small-dense sequences. That was meant to lower p50. Could be interacting with KV eviction and causing serialization stalls in streaming.

owen: I started a quick git bisect on the canary branch. First suspects: commit 8f7d2b1 (kernel autoselect heuristics) and 8f7d2b1's follow-up 8f7d2b3 (prefetch change).

samir: Also worth noting: tool-call serialization path was reworked in PR 4380 to normalize arg ordering; that added an extra copy in edge cases. Could be additive.

jia: Reproduced locally with a mini harness: long-context stream + toolcall heavy workload. When kernel_autoselect is enabled + kv_cache size small, streaming p95 jumps. When I force kernel to the legacy path, the spike disappears.

jia: Repro commands: 
```
# harness (devbox)
./run_stream_harness --model=redwood-small --toolcalls=heavy --kv_size=128 --autoselect=on
# quick toggle
curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/admin/feature?kernel_autoselect=false
```

alyssa: Good repro. Can we confirm whether the KV eviction is causing the eventstream worker to block while it serializes eviction bookkeeping? If so, that would explain bursts.

nowen: Profiling snapshots show lock contention on cache::meta_mutex during heavy toolcall bursts. The serialization goroutine waits for eviction/unlock before writing SSE frames, causing backlog.

samir: That matches the metrics: cache.eviction_count spikes align with stream.write_queue_depth.

alyssa: Action plan: 1) Bisect to the commit that introduced the autoselect heuristic change, 2) revert the heuristic temporarily on canary, 3) add a short-term mutex refinement or switch to try-lock for eviction bookkeeping.

nowen: Bisect output: first bad commit identified at 8f7d2b1 (author: @maria). 8f7d2b1 changes: kernel_autoselect scoring, prefer dense-small kernel when mean_seq_len < 64.

owen: Rolling revert PR -> #4412. Patch: set kernel_autoselect to previous scoring and add telemetry to capture mean_seq_len per request.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #4412 merged to canary, triggering canary redeploy.

deploy-bot: Canary finished redeploy at 2299999150. Healthchecks green.

samir: Post-revert numbers: p95 dropped back ~11% vs broken canary, p50 unchanged. stream.write_queue_depth normalized. Looks promising.

jia: I also instrumented the KV cache to emit try-lock fallback counts. Observed that with the revert, try-lock fallbacks dropped from ~220/s to ~8/s.

alyssa: Good. Next steps: add a targeted unit test that simulates concurrent eviction + streaming serialization to avoid regression, and rework the kernel_autoselect to consider in-flight KV pressure (or default to legacy kernel for streaming requests until select stability verified).

samir: Filed follow-ups: ENG-RT-892 (test harness), ENG-RT-893 (autoselect refinement), ENG-RT-894 (mutex -> try-lock refactor).

owen: I'll request a staging rollout with the candidate autoselect patch that includes instrumentation only (no behavior change) so we can collect telemetry before re-enabling.

alyssa: Thanks all. Marking this thread as a rollout blocker resolved for now. We should capture the full postmortem in incidents/ after we finish the follow-ups.

alyssa: TL;DR: regression introduced by kernel_autoselect heuristic interacting with KV eviction under toolcall-heavy SSE workloads. Reverted on canary (#4412); perf back to baseline; follow-ups created.
